The user just asked: “Oh, also its hitting rate limits. kill them. Why did you start two”. They want to stop the agents that are causing the rate limit errors, and also presumably understand why two agents were started. I’ve already cancelled any live runs earlier (the previous Bash call listed live runs and cancelled them, but there were none). However, the recent runs still show many failures due to HTTP 429 rate limits from the Groq API. Those failures are coming from agents that are still active (or at least their processes are still running) and automatically retrying, causing continued requests and hitting the limit.

To truly stop the flood, I need to pause the agents themselves, not just cancel the current runs. The control plane exposes a `/api/agents/{agentId}/pause` endpoint which will suspend the agent’s background loop. I have the IDs of the agents that have been active in this company: from earlier logs I saw agents with IDs `b5e8d592-2057-4de3-8b9b-936cbb2b60c0` (likely the CEO), `d027bfa7-6d38-412b-94a7-1766519a20da` (the CTO), `3efc82cd-d76d-4183-8d1d-82e3ddb1da6f` (maybe a reviewer), and `c81de09c-c153-46ab-abe0-2305ef729b4d` (the paperclip adapter itself). Pausing all four should halt any further automated calls that are triggering the rate limit.

After pausing, I should verify that there are indeed no live runs remaining. I can query `/api/companies/<CID>/live-runs` and count the entries; expecting zero. I’ll also add a short sleep (e.g., 8 seconds) to give the system time to process the pause requests before checking.

Thus the next step is a Bash command that iterates over the four known agent IDs, sends a POST to the pause endpoint, prints the response name or error and status, then sleeps, then checks live runs count. This matches the pattern used earlier for cancelling runs. I will construct the command accordingly and invoke it via the Bash tool.

The exact command will be:

```
for AID in b5e8d592-2057-4de3-8b9b-936cbb2b60c0 d027bfa7-6d38-412b-94a7-1766519a20da 3efc82cd-d76d-4183-8d1d-82e3ddb1da6f c81de09c-c153-46ab-abe0-2305ef729b4d; do
  curl -s -m10 -X POST "http://localhost:3100/api/agents/$AID/pause" |
    python3 -c "import sys,json;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print(d.get('name') or d.get('error'), d.get('status',''))"
done
sleep 8
curl -s -m5 "http://localhost:3100/api/companies/b9ad5795-5f73-496f-9911-83ebb9e9c48a/live-runs" |
  python3 -c "import sys,json;print(len(json.load(sys.stdin)),'live runs')"
```

That will pause all agents and then confirm there are no live runs.
